## Read in individual environmental data for 200 individuals. Just focus on West, as the East is too divergent and we are curious how SD, West and Southwest vary from each other

```{r}
#env<-read_delim("input/WAVI.env_pland_ndvi.200ind.West_SW_SD_Hyb.csv",delim=",") %>% rename(long=Long,lat=Lat)

# Environment for Western birds, not including any eastern birds of hybrid pops (no eastern birds in Boulder)

pred <- env %>% dplyr::select(EvergreenForest:NDVI_mean) #%>% dplyr::select(-HumanImpact_sum)

# Correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(pred, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# Melt for ggplot

pdf("output/Heatmap.Env_var.inclTree_buff.noHyb.pdf")
```

```{r}
identical(colnames(pred), colnames(cor_matrix))

pred
```

## Genomic data

Create plink ped/map file from imputed vcf file and alter map file so column 2 is snp name (chr.pos). Keep only inds in the GEA. Then recode A, for 0,1,2 genotypes, and then use unix cut command to keep first column (ID) and then all genotypes (from column 7 onwards):

```
cat *raw|cut -f 1,7- -d" "|sed 1d > wavi.200ind.imputed.lfmm.ind_col
```

##PCA is RDA without environment.

We are going to use PCA as the putative population structure. You can also use MEMs if you want.
```{r}
pca <- rda(gen.impall, scale=T)
saveRDS(pca,"WAVI.188ind.pca.noHyb.RDS")
pca<-readRDS("output/WAVI.188ind.pca.noHyb.RDS")

# extract site scores for first 3 PCs
pc_scores <- scores(pca, display = "sites", choices = 1:3)

pdf("output/WAVI.188ind.pca.noHyb.screeplot.pdf")
screeplot(pca, bstick = TRUE)  # broken-stick model helps decide how many axes are meaningful
dev.off()
```

```{r}
coords <- env %>% dplyr::select(Sample, long, lat)
# convert to sf object
coords_sf <- st_as_sf(coords, coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# calculate geodesic distance matrix
geo_dist <- geosphere::distm(as(coords_sf, "Spatial"), fun = geosphere::distHaversine)
dist_mat <- as.dist(geo_dist)

# generate moran's eigenvector maps (MEMs)
mem_positive <- adespatial::dbmem(dist_mat, MEM.autocor = "positive")
 
eigenvalues <- attr(mem_positive, "values")# eigenvalues of the retained MEMs

plot(eigenvalues, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "MEM axis", ylab = "Eigenvalue",
     main = "MEM eigenvalue decay")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
```
```{r}
ggsave("output/WAVI.188.noHyb.MEM_decay_plot.pdf")
```

```{r}
# test MEMs against this reduced genetic summary
mem_rda_test <- rda(pc_scores ~ ., data = as.data.frame(mem_positive))

mem_r2step <- ordiR2step(
  rda(pc_scores ~ 1, data = as.data.frame(mem_positive)),
  scope = formula(mem_rda_test),
  direction = "forward"
)
saveRDS(mem_r2step,"output/WAVI.ForwardSelection.MEM_positive_PCA.RDS")
mem_r2step<-readRDS("output/WAVI.ForwardSel.MEM_positive_on_PCA.RDS")

sig_mems <- attr(mem_r2step$terms, "term.labels")
sig_mems
sig_mems_top<-sig_mems[1:2]

```

## Example of ordiR2step (always forward), 1000 peermutations and p-vaue in 0.01 (pinelodge)
#Parallelizes the 499 permutations at each step# This takes too long, it's better to parallelize permutations within each step for forward selection and maybe we don't need as many permutations
```
mod<-ordiR2step(wavi.mod0,wavi.rda.all,direction="forward",R2permutations=499,Pin=0.01,R2scope=T)  
saveRDS(mod,"output/ForwardSel.CAWA.Env.UncorrectedPop.RDS")
#mod$anova
```
# Parallel permutations within each step- up to this took 350Gb of memory (himem node)
```{r}
fit <- ordiR2step(wavi.mod0, scope = wavi.rda.all,
                  direction="forward",
                  Pin = 0.01,
                  R2scope = TRUE,
                  permutations = how(nperm = 199),
                  parallel = 4)
saveRDS(fit,"output/ForwardSel.WAVI.188ind.West_SW_SD_NoHyb.uncor_env.UncorrectedPop.RDS")

#fit<-readRDS("output/ForwardSel.WAVI.188ind.West_SW_SD_NoHyb.uncor_env.UncorrectedPop.RDS")

# convert the anova table to a data frame
sel_table <- as.data.frame(fit$anova)

# drop the "<All variables>" summary row, keep only actual selection steps
sel_table <- sel_table[rownames(sel_table) != "<All variables>", ]

# variable names have a "+ " prefix — strip it and trim whitespace
selected_vars <- trimws(gsub("^\\+ ", "", rownames(sel_table)))

selected_vars
#> [1] "elev"  "bio10" "qscat" "bio18" "bio15"
```

## Adaptive landscape: projecting adaptive gradient(s) across space
### Plot in PC space the relationship of these variables and the individuals
Note that Brenna plotted the adaptively enriched RDA- we are not subsetting to the super adpative loci, we are using all loci as recommended by Lotteros et al, but we do subset to the variables selected in the forward selection model. For ROFI, we are using top variables from gradient forest to be consistent.

### First get eigenvalues for plot
```{r}
# eigenvalues for each constrained RDA axis
eigenvals <- RDA_outliers$CCA$eig

# sum each set of eigenvalues separately, then add totals
total_inertia <- sum(RDA_outliers$CA$eig) + sum(RDA_outliers$CCA$eig)

# % of total variance for each constrained (RDA) axis
pct_explained <- RDA_outliers$CCA$eig / total_inertia * 100

print(paste('Percent variance explained for each RDA axis'))
pct_explained

# proportion of constrained variance per RDA axis
pct_constrained <- RDA_outliers$CCA$eig / sum(RDA_outliers$CCA$eig) * 100

print(paste('Proportion of constrained variance explained for each RDA axis in a partial RDA'))
pct_constrained
pct1 <- round(pct_constrained[1], 2)
pct2 <- round(pct_constrained[2], 2)

```

## Get candidate loci for 3 standard deviaitons away
### Get snp scores for the constrained axes 1 thorugh num_axes
```{r}
num_axes <- 2
loadings <- scores(RDA_outliers, choices = 1:num_axes, display = "species")

# helper function: find outlier SNPs beyond z standard deviations
find_outliers <- function(x, z = 3) {
  lims <- mean(x) + c(-1, 1) * z * sd(x) # threshold: mean ± z*sd
  x[x < lims[1] | x > lims[2]]           # return SNPs outside limits
}

# identify outlier SNPs for each axis
outlier_list <- lapply(1:num_axes, function(ax) {
  vals <- loadings[, ax]
  snps <- find_outliers(vals, z = 3)
  data.frame(
    axis     = ax,
    snp      = names(snps),
    loading  = unname(snps),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

# combine into one dataframe
outliers_df <- do.call(rbind, outlier_list)

#  total number of candidate SNPs
n_candidates <- nrow(outliers_df)
cat("Number of candidate SNPs:", n_candidates, "\n")
```

## Calculate correlations of candidate SNPs with predictors assuming your predictors are in a matrix/dataframe 'pred2'
```{r}
#selected_vars<-c("elev", "bio10" ,"qscat", "bio18", "bio15")
predictors <- pred2[selected_vars]
cor_mat <- matrix(nrow = n_candidates, ncol = ncol(predictors))
colnames(cor_mat) <- colnames(predictors)

for (i in 1:n_candidates) {
  snp_name <- outliers_df$snp[i]
  snp_gen  <- gen.impall[, snp_name]
  cor_mat[i, ] <- apply(predictors, 2, function(x) cor(x, snp_gen))
}

cand <- cbind(outliers_df, cor_mat)

# remove SNPs detected on multiple axes
cand <- cand[!duplicated(cand$snp), ]

# identify which predictor each SNP is most strongly correlated with
predictor_cols <- colnames(predictors)

cand$predictor <- apply(cand[, predictor_cols], 1, function(row) {
  predictor_cols[which.max(abs(row))]
})

cand$correlation <- apply(cand[, predictor_cols], 1, function(row) {
  max(abs(row))
})

# print number of SNPs per predictor
table(cand$predictor)

cand$snp2 <- sub("_[ACGT]$", "", cand$snp)
cand$CHROM <- paste0(sub("RagTag.*$", "", cand$snp2, "RagTag"))
cand$POS   <- sub(".*RagTag\\.", "", cand$snp2)

#.* — greedily matches everything from the start of the string
saveRDS(cand, "candidate_snps_with_correlation.chrom_pos_fixed.RDS")

candidate_snps <- cand$snp
#saveRDS(candidate_snps, "candidate_snps_noci.RDS")

cand_pos <- t(sapply(candidate_snps, function(x) {
  # split chrom vs position/allele by pattern in scaffold name
  #This is robust to however many periods precede RagTag, since it's anchored to the literal string rather than counting delimiter positions.
  if (!grepl("RagTag", x)) {
    cat("Problem SNP (no 'RagTag'):", x, "\n")
    return(c(CHROM = NA, POS = NA))
  }
  
  chrom <- paste0(sub("RagTag.*$", "", x), "RagTag")
  pos_allele <- sub(".*RagTag\\.", "", x)
  
  # extract numeric position before underscore
  pos <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(str_split(pos_allele, "_")[[1]][1]))
  
  if (is.na(pos)) {
    cat("Could not parse position for SNP:", x, "\n")
  }
  
  c(CHROM = chrom, POS = pos)
}))

# convert to data frame
cand_pos <- as.data.frame(cand_pos, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cand_pos$POS <- as.integer(cand_pos$POS)



cat("Number of NA positions:", sum(is.na(cand_pos$POS)), "\n")
print(head(cand_pos, 10))

# write out
write_tsv(cand_pos, "WAVI.188ind.noHyb.candidate_adaptive_snps_subset.tsv", col_names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
## P-values threshold after Bonferroni correction
thres_env <- 0.01/length(rdadapt_env$p.values)

## Identifying the loci that are below the p-value threshold
outliers <- data.frame(Loci = colnames(gen.impall)[which(rdadapt_env$p.values<thres_env)], p.value = rdadapt_env$p.values[which(rdadapt_env$p.values<thres_env)], contig = unlist(lapply(strsplit(colnames(gen.impall)[which(rdadapt_env$p.values<thres_env)], split = "_"), function(x) x[1]))) 
head(outliers)
```

#keeping all loci per contig (not narrowing it down to one per contig)
```{r}
outliers <- outliers[order(outliers$contig, outliers$p.value), ]

outliers$snp <- sub("_[ACGT]$", "", outliers$Loci)
#outliers$CHROM <- sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", outliers$snp) # remove the final ".xxxx" segment
#outliers$POS   <- sub(".*\\.", "", outliers$snp) # keep only what's after the final "."
outliers$CHROM <- paste0(sub("RagTag.*$", "", outliers$snp), "RagTag")
outliers$POS   <- sub(".*RagTag\\.", "", outliers$snp)
dim(outliers)

write.table(outliers,"output/WAVI.188ind.noHyb.outlier_BonferroniCorr.pvalue.loci.txt",row.names=F,quote=F,sep="\t")
```

## Partial RDA conditioning on MEM
```{r}
env_terms <- paste(selected_vars, collapse = " + ")  # your env vars from ordiR2step earlier
cond_terms <- paste(sig_mems, collapse = " + ")

partial_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("gen.impall ~", env_terms, "+ Condition(", cond_terms, ")")
)

partial_rda <- rda(partial_formula, data = env_data_mem)
```
## Variance partitioning
```{r}
# environmental effect after conditioning out space
RsquareAdj(partial_rda)

# variance partitioning: pure environment, pure space, shared, unexplained
# build formulas as strings, then convert to formula objects
env_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(selected_vars, collapse = " + ")))
spatial_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(sig_mems_top, collapse = " + ")))

# run varpart with dynamically built formulas
varpart_result <- varpart(
  gen.impall,           # or gen.impall / your genetic response matrix
  env_formula,
  spatial_formula,
  data = env_data_mem    # data frame containing both env vars and MEM columns
)
saveRDS(varpart_result,"WAVI.188ind.NoHyb.exclLD.VarPart.Env_SelMEM.RDS")

pdf("WAVI.188ind.NoHyb.exclLD.VarPart.Env_SelMEM.pdf")
plot(varpart_result)
dev.off()

print(paste('Ran and saved VarPart for selected environmental variables and top MEMs'))

```


```{r}
# eigenvalues for each constrained RDA axis
eigenvalsP <- partial_rda$CCA$eig

# sum each set of eigenvalues separately, then add totals
total_inertiaP <- sum(partial_rda$CA$eig) + sum(partial_rda$CCA$eig)

# % of total variance for each constrained (RDA) axis
pct_explainedP <- partial_rda$CCA$eig / total_inertiaP * 100

print(paste('Percent variance explained for each RDA axis in a partial RDA'))
pct_explainedP

# proportion of constrained variance per RDA axis
pct_constrainedP <- partial_rda$CCA$eig / sum(partial_rda$CCA$eig) * 100

print(paste('Proportion of constrained variance explained for each RDA axis in a partial RDA'))
pct_constrainedP
pct1 <- round(pct_constrainedP[1], 2)
pct2 <- round(pct_constrainedP[2], 2)

```
